messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: mirt version 0.9.0 on CRAN
parts:
Hi all,

Next release has been sent to CRAN and looks to be built for all platforms. Check the NEWS file for a description of the user visible updates and new features, the most annoying and code breaking of which is the removal of the confmirt() and confmirt.model() functions, which have been replaced by a method = 'MHRM' argument in the mirt() function and mirt.model(). 

Additionally, I've made a neat interactive tool via the 'shiny' package that provides a wrapper to the itemplot() function, which might be useful for understanding how mirt parametrizes various items types, and what happens to other dependent item functions (like expected item lines, information trace lines, etc). You can load the utility after installing the shiny package by using 

> shiny::runGist('6337165')  

Cheers.

Phil

messages.author: 885539f3f5ae8fd5
messages.subject: Re: mirt version 0.9.0 on CRAN
parts: This is a really cool feature of the package. I played around with the code a bit so that the sliders for the different parameter values use the "traditional" IRT parameterization, to help the students in the lab I'm TAing get a feel for how the traditional parameterization values can affect the trace lines. I'm trying to extent the graph a bit on the x-axis though -- I'd like to have something around xlim(-5,5) but I tried that and it only widened the graph without actually showing more of the trace lines. Can you tell me where I should be looking to modify this feature? Thanks in advance! (P.S. I'm not distributing anything I do -- I'm not at all trying to steal credit or anything like that, it's just for educational purposes.)

messages.subject: Re: mirt version 0.9.0 on CRAN
parts:
Hi Jon,

You are the second person to ask for this feature this week, so I've
pushed it to the dev version with a new input called theta_lim for
specifying the lower and upper range to be evaluated. Also, if you've
adapted the shiny gui to work with the classical IRT parameters then
feel free to send a pull request on Github (especially if you provide
an additional checkbox to enable this feature similar the
multidimensional checkbox currently provided). Cheers.

Phil
